summary:
Implemented the Tabs feature in the repo, but nothing has been run: per your instruction, tests and repository code were not executed, so all checks were by reading only.

Changes:
- src/textual/widgets/tabs.py (new): Tab, TabsRenderable, Tabs. Tabs uses DEFAULT_STYLES = "height: 2;", a watch__active_tab_name watcher that animates _bar_position, and an async on_key with the specified key rules.
- src/textual/renderables/underline_bar.py: clickable_ranges added before width; renders one Text object; click spans appended last in mapping order; zero-width early path adds none.
- src/textual/renderables/opacity.py: blended color merged into each segment's existing style, preserving meta.
- docs/reference/tabs.md: single ::: textual.widgets.tabs.Tabs directive.
- sandbox/tabs_demo.py and sandbox/tabs_demo.css: demo mounting two Tabs on the App.
- tests/renderables/test_underline_bar.py: three tests appended; existing tests untouched.
- tests/widgets/test_tabs.py and tests/widgets/__init__.py (new): Tabs behavior tests.

Choices: the layout resolver already declares size, fraction, and min_size on its Edge protocol, so it was left unchanged. Only padding edges go through the resolver, with label widths subtracted first, which gives the same result and avoids treating zero-width labels as flexible. First-character search only fires for single-character keys.

Known issue: bar position uses the full-list index from find_tab_by_name, as the spec requires, but the underline is drawn over displayed (deduplicated) tabs. With duplicate names the two indices diverge, so the underline can sit on the wrong tab. Indices wrap modulo the displayed count, so it does not error. Fixing this would contradict the spec's stated initial-state rule.

No commits were made.
